videos.script:
You have been writing for of loops since lesson 4. {{forof}} Over arrays, over the entries of a Map, over a string. But what does for of actually ask of the thing it loops over?

One method, with a strange name. {{protocol}} Anything that has it can be looped over, spread into an array, and destructured. Arrays have it, strings have it, Maps and Sets have it. Plain objects do not, which is why looping over one fails.

{{custom}} Today you will give that method to your own objects, so a range of numbers can be looped over like an array. {{generator}} Then generators: functions that can stop in the middle, hand back a value, and carry on later from exactly where they stopped.

That sounds abstract. {{lazy}} What it buys is laziness. A generator can describe an infinite list of numbers, and only the ones you actually take are ever produced. {{async}} And the same idea, waiting between values, is how a program reads pages from a server one at a time, which is where the next lessons are heading.
